artboards.title: Home — what you have made, and who is worth a visit
Sell — every line says what you take home on it
Order — the close, and what it puts in your pocket

annotations.text:
FIELD — the agent's app

I was designing for the wrong person. The console's rules — one accent, no depth, ink instead of colour, nothing decorative — are the OWNER's rules, for a man at a desk reconciling books. An agent is a commission salesman standing in somebody's yard. The app has to make him want to sell.

So the rules are off. What stays is the identity: the oxide red, Archivo Black, Inter, IBM Plex Mono.

THREE DECISIONS

1. MONEY IS THE FIRST THING AND THE BIGGEST THING. The app opens on what he has earned this month at 44px, with the gap to HIS OWN BEST MONTH underneath — not a target somebody set for him. 47,800 to beat it, about two orders. That is a reason to go out this afternoon.

2. WHAT HE EARNS IS ON EVERY PRODUCT. The old app showed a floor price and left him to work his cut out in his head, which is why the easy-money lines went unsold. Now every row carries "3,800 to you", and a bonus line carries "+2,500 to you" in the brand red. He can see, at a glance, which shelf pays him.

3. THE ORDER RIDES WITH HIM. A dark bar at the foot of the selling screen, carrying the total AND his cut, so it is never scrolled away while he is adding to it. At the close, the tally goes dark like the hero and his earnings are the largest figure on the screen, in the good colour.

WHAT ELSE CHANGED

  Dark earnings surface, warm — oxide bled into the black, one soft
  bloom behind the figure. Not a flat grey page.
  Cards at 18px radius with real shadows, floating on a light ground.
  Archivo Black for money moments; Plex Mono for anything tabular.
  Two greens, because one cannot serve both grounds: mint reads 10.7:1
  on the hero and 1.9:1 on paper, so paper gets the deep verdigris.

Every pair on these screens clears AA — including the two that did not
until I measured them: the meta ink was 4.34:1 on this lighter page, and
the inactive tab labels were 2.59:1.

NEXT, IF THIS IS RIGHT: Clients, the money detail behind the hero, and
the states — day one, and a read that failed.
